description.narrative: Colombia plays a key role for many neotropical migratory birds. However, with more than 70% of original forest cover in the tropical Andes already reduced, there is growing recognition that preservation of natural habitats in the tropical Andean forest zone must be coupled with sound management of working landscapes, as this is where most remnants of natural forest are found. The project's goal is to contribute to creating more bird friendly agroecosystems in working landscapes in the Inter-Andean slopes of Cauca Valley of Colombia. This goal will be met by aiding in providing habitats and maintaining landscape connectivity and working together within local communities to plan for bird friendly spaces within working landscapes. Specifically, the grantee will work with local farmers who will build and maintain a native plants nursery in each location selected. Likewise, local community will be involved in workshops and meetings that educate farmers and their families how to design bird friendly gardens, and other bird-friendly practices. ..Species that will benefit include: yellow-billed cuckoo, olive-sided flycatcher, eastern wood-pewee, Acadian flycatcher, barn swallow, Swainson's thrush, golden-winged warbler, cerulean warbler, Canada warbler, Blackburnian warbler, black-and-white warbler, mourning warbler, summer tanager and rose-breasted grosbeak.....
